Header: Phyllophaga spp. Heteronychus spp. Marindi (Embu-Kenya), Amakonde (Ekegusii-Kenya) Kegunyo (Kikuyu), Mogonyonik (Nandi) Ofunyo (Dholuo) Kamasibili (Luhya)

Prevention: Remove all plant debris and weeds before planting.
Plough and harrow the field to expose eggs and grubs to predators and desiccation by the sun.
Ensure proper nutrition for a healthy crop for vigorous growth.
Ensure proper drainage to discourage multiplication of the pest.
Rotate with non-host plants such as sunflower, cabbages, Irish potatoes, sweet potatoes, etc.
Use properly decomposed manure during planting.
Cattle should not graze in field as the manure may attract the chafer grubs who will lay eggs in the manure.
Monitoring: Additional relevant crops: sorghum, millet, wheat, Napier grass, tobacco, potatoes, tomatoes, groundnuts, cabbages, etc.
C-shaped larva with a brown head and three pairs of legs in the crop field.
Scout for the larvae during the vegatative growth of the plants.
Larvae in the soil as they feed on the roots of plants.
Wilting of plants, irregular growth of crop, patches of tilted or lodged plants.
Initiate control measures when 2 grubs are found per cubic foot (i.e. 60 x 30 x 15 cm).
Direct Control: Prune trees around the crop that attract adults beetles.
Burn or destroy pruned limbs/ stems to kill the adults.
Shake trees that harbour adult beetles for collection and destruction by burning.
Visible larvae can also be picked and destroyed as well.
Restrictions: Follow label instructions on the product
Always consult recent list of registered pesticides
Ensure safe disposal of empty containers
The below pesticides should be sprayed to the soil near the 1
2 week old maize crop to kill the larvae which stays in the soil
Chemical control is rarely necessary for chafer grubs.
II, Moderately hazardous; PHI 14 days; MRLs 1.0mgs/kg;
Mida 200SL at the rate of 10mls/20L of water, Confidor 200SL at the rate of 10mls/20L of water etc.)
